title: The MCP authorization flow
lede: A client calls an MCP server with no token, reads the 401 challenge, follows it to the protected resource metadata and the authorization server metadata, runs authorization code with PKCE, and meets the scope check. Simulated: the targets are in-process mock servers.

nodes.label: 1 MCP client
sub: Calls the MCP endpoint with no token.

nodes.label: 2 MCP server
sub: Answers 401 with a Bearer challenge: resource_metadata and scope.

nodes.label: 4 Auth server metadata
sub: RFC 8414 or OIDC discovery: endpoints, S256, iss support.

nodes.label: 6 Scope check
sub: Token with enough scope: 200. Too little: 403 insufficient_scope.

steps.title: No token, 401
steps.what: The client calls the MCP endpoint with no token. The server answers 401 and the challenge points at its metadata.

steps.title: Protected resource metadata
steps.what: The client fetches protected resource metadata and learns the authorization server.

steps.title: Authorization server metadata
steps.what: It reads the authorization server metadata: endpoints, S256 and iss support.

steps.title: Authorize and token
steps.what: It runs authorization code with PKCE S256, the resource parameter and the iss check.

steps.title: Read token, write tool: 403
steps.what: A read token calls a write tool: 403 insufficient_scope names the scope to step up to.

steps.title: After step-up
steps.what: After step-up the call is allowed.
